create.name: San Francisco Zen Center
create.bio:
San Francisco Zen Center is a Soto Zen community whose founder was the Japanese teacher Shunryu Suzuki Roshi, who died in 1971 and whose talks still shape the way it practises. Its stated purpose is to make the wisdom and compassion of the Buddha available and to live them out, treating formal sitting and everyday activity as equal expressions of the bodhisattva path, and honouring lay and monastic life alike. It looks after three practice places: City Center, an urban temple on Page Street in the middle of San Francisco; Green Gulch Farm, an organic farm and garden in a coastal valley in Marin County; and Tassajara, a monastery and retreat centre deep in the Ventana Wilderness, bought after a fundraising drive that began in November 1966.

A large residential community trains at all three sites, and the centre sees preparing future Zen teachers as part of its core work. For those further away, SFZC Online runs a daily online zendo with live zazen, chanting and talks that are free and need no sign-up, along with weekly drop-in sessions with teachers, live courses on Buddhist texts and practice, and self-paced recorded study. An extensive archive of Dharma talks from its teachers and guests is open to everyone, and a network of affiliated groups, Branching Streams, carries the lineage further afield.

courses.title: The Zen of Poetry and the Poetry of Zen, Online 11/16–12/21
courses.description: A six-week Monday morning course on Zoom with Koji Vanessa Able, reading old Chinese and Japanese Buddhist verse beside modern poets and trying short guided writing exercises on themes such as nature, perception and not-knowing. Newcomers to poetry are welcome.
courses.price: Benefactor $420; Standard $336; Member $302; Supported $202; Deeply Supported $84

free_resources.title: Online Zendo and Livestream Practice
free_resources.description: SFZC Online's hub: livestreamed daily zazen, chanting, ceremonies and Dharma talks that are free with no registration, plus links to drop-in practice sessions with teachers.

free_resources.title: Entering Practice
free_resources.description: A starting point for newcomers: recorded zazen instruction from several teachers, a beginners' reading list, temple sounds, films of Suzuki Roshi and a recorded class series on Buddhist and Zen basics.
